facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: These studies are aimed at identification of possible new impact structures, verification of their origin, and detailed analysis of the geological structure and rock deformation in such crater structures. However, these are rare features on the surface of the Earth and only 190 structures are currently known and accepted as confirmed impact structures... out of which three confirmed impact structures are from India (e.g. Lonar, Dhala and Ramgarh craters).
facts.text: The Geological Survey of India documented shock-metamorphic textures, including the transformation of plagioclase into maskelynite, confirming that the Lonar depression was formed by a hypervelocity meteorite impact in basalt.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The crater is a circular depression with 1.83 kms in diameter and 150 meters in depth with a shallow lake at the bottom.
facts.text: The Lonar crater depression measures approximately 1.83 kilometres in rim diameter and 150 metres in depth.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: It was notified as a National Geo-heritage Monument in 1979 by Geological Survey of India (GSI).
facts.text: The Geological Survey of India declared the Lonar impact structure a National Geo-heritage Monument in 1979.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: The age of the crater is usually estimated to be 52,000 ± 6,000 years (Sengupta et al, 1997, Siddiqi, S. Z., 2008, Babar, S. M., 2010); although a study published in 2010 gives an age of 570,000 ± 47,000 years (Jourdan, F., 2011).
facts.text: Scientists disagree on the impact age of the Lonar crater, with thermoluminescence dating suggesting roughly 52,000 years ago while argon-argon dating indicates an age of approximately 570,000 years.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: The Archaeological Survey of India currently oversees the protection and conservation of the Daitya Sudan Temple as part of a broader effort to preserve the Lonar crater's cultural heritage.
facts.text: The Archaeological Survey of India protects the Daitya Sudan Temple at Lonar, a medieval stone shrine built in the Hemadpanthi architectural style.

facts.label: archaeology
facts.quote: Measuring approximately 32 metres in length and 25.8 metres in breadth, the temple is arranged in an irregular star-shaped plan — a characteristic Hemadpanthi device.
facts.text: Architectural documentation of the Daitya Sudan Temple records its perimeter structure as roughly 32 metres in length and 25.8 metres in breadth.

facts.label: disputed
facts.quote: The Daitya Sudan Temple, dating broadly to the 12th 14th centuries CE and reflecting the patronage of both the later Chalukyas and the Devagiri Yadavas, is the best-preserved structure of the Lonar Crater Temple Complex.
facts.text: Scholars debate the foundational period of the Daitya Sudan Temple, with some attributing its initial design to the Western Chalukya dynasty while others ascribe its standing architecture to the 12th to 13th century Yadava dynasty.
